title: India's Biggest Healthcare IPO Is Coming — Manipal Health Just Got SEBI's Green Light for a $1.2 Billion Listing
excerpt: The Temasek-backed hospital chain, which runs 48 hospitals and more than 12,000 beds across 14 states, is targeting a late July debut that will test investor appetite for India's booming private healthcare sector.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Manipal Health's IPO could raise up to $1.2 billion, marking a significant healthcare listing in India.
  • The company operates 48 hospitals with over 12,600 beds across 14 states, making it a major player.
  • India's private healthcare sector is experiencing double-digit revenue growth driven by rising incomes and insurance penetration.
  • The IPO will test investor confidence amid a recovering market and a busy second half for listings.
  • Manipal's concentration in Karnataka poses a risk, as it generates nearly 50% of its revenue from the state.

Manipal Health Enterprises, India's second-largest private hospital chain by scale, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering, two people familiar with the development told Reuters on Friday. The company is targeting a market debut in late July or early August, in what is expected to be one of the largest healthcare IPOs in Indian history. The offering, filed in March, comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth ₹8,000 crore (roughly $850 million) and an offer for sale of up to 4.32 crore shares by promoters and existing investors, including Singapore's Temasek Holdings, TPG, and Novo Holdings. At the upper end, the total raise could approach $1.2 billion, valuing the company at approximately $13 billion. The listing comes at a pivotal moment for India's capital markets. After a turbulent first half marked by the US-Israeli conflict with Iran, a record $29 billion selloff by foreign portfolio investors, and a sharp correction in benchmark indices, sentiment has begun to recover. The Sensex has reclaimed 77,000 and the Nifty 50 has pushed above 24,200, with oil prices retreating below $71 per barrel and early signs of a US-Iran peace framework supporting risk appetite. ## Why Manipal Matters Manipal Health operates a pan-India network of 48 hospitals with over 12,367 licensed beds spanning 14 states and union territories. The launch of its 49th hospital in Bengaluru pushed capacity to 12,631 beds, and its acquisition of Sahyadri Hospitals in late 2025 added 1,606 beds, strengthening its presence in western India. By bed capacity, it is India's largest pan-India multispecialty hospital network; by number of facilities, it ranks second among private chains, according to CRISIL. > **"A pre-IPO placement of up to ₹1,600 crore may reduce the fresh issue size if completed."** The company plans to use the fresh capital primarily to repay ₹5,378 crore of outstanding debt at subsidiary Manipal Hospitals Private Limited, acquire a minority stake in step-down subsidiary Sahyadri Hospitals (₹574 crore), and fund general corporate purposes. A pre-IPO placement of up to ₹1,600 crore may reduce the fresh issue size if completed. Kotak Mahindra Capital, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, JP Morgan, UBS Securities India, and DBS Bank are managing the issue — a heavyweight roster that underscores the significance of the offering. ![Temasek Holdings — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a8/The_Atrium_%40_Orchard.JPG) ## The Healthcare Investment Thesis India's private healthcare sector is in the middle of a structural transformation. Rising incomes, expanding insurance penetration, growing chronic disease burden, and a cultural shift toward private hospitals for complex care are all driving double-digit revenue growth across the listed hospital chains. Apollo Hospitals, Max Healthcare, and Narayana Health have all seen their stock prices multiply over the past three years, rewarding investors who bet early on the sector.
Market Context for Manipal's IPO
›IPO could raise up to $1.2 billion.
›Sensex reclaimed 77,000; Nifty 50 above 24,200.
›Net foreign purchases of ₹13.6 billion on July 3.
›Healthcare sector experiencing double-digit growth.
Manipal's listing will give public market investors exposure to a hospital operator with significant scale, a diversified geographic footprint, and a proven acquisition playbook. However, its concentration in Karnataka — which accounted for nearly 50 percent of revenue in the first half of FY26 — is a point to watch. Eighteen of its hospitals and 6,040 of its beds are in the state. ## What It Means for the NRI Investor For diaspora investors watching India's equity markets, the Manipal IPO sits at the intersection of two powerful trends: India's healthcare boom and its resurgent IPO pipeline. The second half of 2026 is shaping up to be the busiest IPO season in years, with Jio Platforms' $3.8 billion listing, the National Stock Exchange's ₹30,000 crore debut, Carlsberg India's confidential filing, and now Manipal all in the queue. The healthcare angle carries particular resonance for NRIs. Many diaspora Indians rely on Indian hospital networks for planned surgeries and medical tourism, drawn by the combination of world-class clinical expertise and dramatically lower costs. Manipal's facilities in Bengaluru, Goa, and Delhi are among the most visited by overseas patients. Investing in the IPO offers a way to participate financially in a sector that many NRIs already experience as consumers. At the same time, the IPO will test whether global investors' renewed interest in Indian equities — which saw net foreign purchases of ₹13.6 billion on July 3 alone — extends beyond index heavyweights to large new listings in sectors that are less exposed to the AI-driven volatility rattling tech-heavy markets in South Korea and Taiwan. The road to listing will also be a barometer for market confidence. If Manipal prices well and lists strong, it could open the floodgates for the rest of H2 2026's IPO pipeline. If it stumbles, the message will be that geopolitical caution still outweighs India's growth story — at least for now. **Sources:** Reuters; The Hindu Business Line; LiveMint; CRISIL.
